title: Transition
description: `<root>/.claude/exchange/handoffs/<id>/<after>-<suffix>.json`. One status change, in its own file, because the session that makes a change is not the session that posted the handoff and two writers sharing one file is how an entry gets lost. The handoff id is the directory name and is deliberately not repeated in here: a second copy of it could disagree with the first, and this repo keeps finding that exact shape.

at.description: When the move was made. For reading, never for ordering: the clock here records seconds, and the first version of this file did order by it - accepting and then closing a handoff inside one second produced two moves with the same timestamp and a reader that picked between them by random suffix, which read the handoff back as accepted after it was closed. `after` is the ordering.

after.description: How many moves this one was written after - the number its writer read before deciding. That makes it a causal position rather than a clock reading: moves made one after another strictly increase, and two writers that both acted on the same state both land on the same number, which is the honest answer because they were concurrent. The filename leads with it for legibility; the ordering is read from here, so there is no width at which padding stops sorting.

status.description: Where it moved to. Accepting is explicitly not closing: a lane taking ownership is not the work being finished, and an accepted handoff with no later closure is exactly the state that should stay visible.

by.description: Who moved it, when that is known.

note.description: Why, in their words. Never parsed.
